sections.heading: The four phases
points: Fetch: PC -> MAR, memory read, result -> MDR -> IR, and PC incremented.
Decode: the control unit reads the opcode and works out the operands.
Execute: the ALU or the memory does the actual work.
Interrupt check: only after execute, never in the middle of it.

sections.heading: Registers worth knowing by name
points: PC  - address of the NEXT instruction.
IR  - the current instruction, still encoded.
MAR - the address being put on the address bus.
MDR - the data travelling to or from memory.

sections.heading: Traps the quiz likes
points: The PC is incremented during fetch, before anyone knows it was a jump.
A jump works by overwriting the PC during execute.
An interrupt never splits an instruction in half.
